 Ground the main conductor.

Switch off the power supply to the control circuit and exhaust the compressed 
 air from the drain valve of the air reservoir.

Evacuate the sf6 gas and ventilate the inside of the enclosures carefully 
 before internal inspection.

Be sure to insert the closing or tripping preventative pins at the time of 
 internal inspection and inspection of moving parts.
Do not smear the lubricant on the insulators.

Renew all the O-rings at the flanges which have been opened for inspection. 
 Handle O-rings with special care to avoid any damage.
Do not disassemble the slide seal assemblies.

Replace the absorbent after the inspection inside enclosure is finished. 
 Replacement should be done just before the evacuation of the air inside the 
 enclosure.
Tighten each bolt with a proper torque.
Test the leakage of all reassembled gas seals.

Compare the mechanical operation data obtained before and after the inspection 
 to insure orderly operation of the breaker.

DON'T OPERATE THE CIRCUIT BREAKER BY THE PNEUMATIC OPERATING MECHANISM WHEN 
 THE SF6 GAS PRESSURE IN THE ENCLOSURES IS BELOW THE LOCK PRESSURE

text:
Power 
 Stations | Technical 
 Procedure
Introduction
This inspection details the items which are inspected after a predetermined 
 permissible number of operations or when some abnormal behavior is found.
The necessary parts of the breaker should be inspected by a special inspection 
 program.
The first draft is initiated by eng. Sherif Mahrous Omar tested by eng. Nafad 
 Kamel Mahmoud, revised by UEEPCO. Quality control general director eng. Gamal 
 Abd Elwahab, accepted by technical expert eng. Hassan Elbehiry and approved by 
 eng. Mohamed Gamal Diab Head sector of El-Kuriemat power station.
Safety Precautions
Open the circuit breaker and open the DS's at both sides of the breaker pole. 
 Ground the main conductor.
Switch off the power supply to the control circuit and exhaust the compressed 
 air from the drain valve of the air reservoir.
Evacuate the sf6 gas and ventilate the inside of the enclosures carefully 
 before internal inspection.
Be sure to insert the closing or tripping preventative pins at the time of 
 internal inspection and inspection of moving parts.
Use designated lubricant.
Do not smear the lubricant on the insulators.
Renew all the O-rings at the flanges which have been opened for inspection. 
 Handle O-rings with special care to avoid any damage.
Do not disassemble the slide seal assemblies.
Replace the absorbent after the inspection inside enclosure is finished. 
 Replacement should be done just before the evacuation of the air inside the 
 enclosure.
Tighten each bolt with a proper torque.
Test the leakage of all reassembled gas seals.
Compare the mechanical operation data obtained before and after the inspection 
 to insure orderly operation of the breaker.
DON'T OPERATE THE CIRCUIT BREAKER BY THE PNEUMATIC OPERATING MECHANISM WHEN 
 THE SF6 GAS PRESSURE IN THE ENCLOSURES IS BELOW THE LOCK PRESSURE
Environmental Recommendations
Fix any oil leaks from shock absorber oil to prevent pollution and save money 
 of wasted oil. Oil leaks to the ground have very bad impacts on the 
 environment, mainly on soil and ground water and eventually on the ecosystem.
"It takes only I liter of Hydrocarbon spilled in an aquifer to render 1,000,000 
liters of potable water useless for human consumption"
Tools and Equipment
220V ac supply.
Portable pressure gauge.
Emergency light.
Timing equipment.
Work to be carried out
When the breaker has operated for a predetermined number of operations indicated 
in the following table, the arc contacts and nozzles should be renewed 
irrespective of wear or erosion.
Interrupting current | Permissible operation numbers
Rated interrupting current | Approx. 20 times
Rated normal current | Approx 2000 times
Small current 
 (about several hundred amperes) | Approx. 4000 times
Permissible operation numbers of the C.B
Name of parts | Service limit
Stationary arc contact | The tip of the stationary arc contact wears more than 2mm or is chipped 
 significantly.
Moving arc contact | The tip of the moving arc contact wears more than 2mm or is chipped 
 significantly.
Nozzles | The diameter of the nozzle throat is enlarged to more than 1mm or the 
 nozzle is significantly flaked.
